identification: Sheet of 20 Australian pennies and halfpennies in 2x2 holders with handwritten variety notes. Photo shows 1922 'Indian die' (worn, looks F to VF, dull brown, not Mint State), 1920 penny in a barcoded dealer holder (note says double dot, cannot be read from photo), 1959 plain, 1942I, 1948P, 1964Y, 1951 etc. Mostly common dates with flan flaws; the sheet value rests on the 1922 Indian and 1920 double dot, which are attributed only by the previous owner/dealer notes.

viewing_check: Take the 1922 and 1920 coins out of their holders: photograph both faces of each. 1922 Indian die needs the obverse rim and lettering and the grade (looks F-VF). The 1920 needs the two dots below the scroll (six clear pearls) and whether it is genuinely the double dot or a plain 1920. Also check the 1948P A1178 and 1942I flaw coins for real errors (not just wear).
market_summary: Realistic resale for the whole sheet looks about $100-250 if the two key pennies are genuine but circulated: a circulated 1922 Indian is roughly $20-60 and a circulated 1920 double dot $40-225 depending on grade. Mixed variety lots at Noble sold $70-240. The previous Gowans sheet went for $50.
